question: Roughly what percentage of waste coming out of a healthcare facility is actually considered hazardous?

options.A: 75 to 90 percent
options.B: 10 to 25 percent
options.C: 50 to 60 percent
options.D: 95 to 99 percent

explanation: Most hospital waste is regular everyday trash (like office paper and food wrappers). Only about 10 to 25 percent is truly hazardous and needs special handling. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h1)

question: Why is throwing away medical waste improperly such a big danger to people living outside the hospital?

options.A: It immediately increases the cost of municipal electricity bills
options.B: It can contaminate local water supplies and soil with pathogens and chemicals
options.C: It triggers loud community noise pollution during night hours
options.D: It causes immediate structural damage to residential homes

explanation: When hazardous waste isn't contained properly, dangerous germs and chemicals can leak into the soil and water where the local community lives and farms. Safety starts with proper disposal! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h1)

question: What is the single most important step in managing hospital waste safely?

options.A: Segregation
options.B: Compacting
options.C: Exporting
options.D: Incineration

explanation: Sorting or segregating your waste right at the bedside is key! If you separate things correctly from the start, every step that follows becomes much safer and easier. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h2)

question: What happens if hazardous waste accidentally gets thrown into the same bin as ordinary office paper?

options.A: The local municipal workers will sort it out safely at the dump
options.B: The total volume of waste instantly decreases by half
options.C: The entire combined batch must be treated as hazardous waste
options.D: The office paper automatically sterilizes the hazardous waste

explanation: Once clean and hazardous waste mix, you can no longer separate them safely. The whole bag now has to be treated as hazardous waste, which costs more and increases risk! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h2)

question: In Nigeria, what color of bin liner is normally used for ordinary, non-hazardous general waste?

options.A: Brown
options.B: Black
options.C: Red
options.D: Yellow

explanation: Black bins and liners are standard for general municipal-type waste that carries no infectious risk. Easy to remember for your clinical rotations! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h3)

question: As a nurse giving injections in a clinic, up to what level should you fill your safety box before sealing it?

options.A: Only half full to save space
options.B: Packed tightly by pressing down with a hand
options.C: Three-quarters full
options.D: Filled completely to the absolute brim

explanation: Never overfill a sharps box! Sealing it when it's three-quarters full keeps everyone safe from accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h3)

question: What major environmental problem is caused by poorly operated, low-temperature medical incinerators?

options.A: Complete disappearance of municipal electricity grids
options.B: Release of toxic dioxins and furans into the air
options.C: Immediate flooding of nearby hospital wards
options.D: Excessive production of harmless oxygen gas

explanation: Burning medical waste at low temperatures without proper filters releases nasty chemical pollutants like dioxins and furans into our air. High standards matter! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h4)

question: Why do hospitals still rely on high-temperature incineration for certain waste, despite environmental concerns?

options.A: It is the only method permitted for ordinary kitchen food leftovers
options.B: It transforms dangerous clinical trash into reusable office furniture
options.C: It requires zero financial investment to build and maintain
options.D: It completely destroys difficult pathological waste and reduces overall volume

explanation: Some body tissues and heavy clinical waste need intense heat to completely and permanently wipe out disease risks. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h4)

question: What primary agent does an autoclave use to disinfect infectious medical waste?

options.A: Open flame combustion
options.B: High-pressure saturated steam
options.C: Concentrated liquid bleach
options.D: Ultraviolet sun rays

explanation: Autoclaves use intense, high-pressure steam to kill germs effectively without needing to burn the materials. A staple equipment in healthcare! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h5)

question: What is the main reason infectious waste is shredded after going through microwave treatment?

options.A: To render the waste unrecognizable and reduce its physical volume
options.B: To reactivate dormant bacterial spores for laboratory testing
options.C: To separate plastic components from metal parts manually
options.D: To increase the weight of the bags before final transport

explanation: Shredding ensures nobody can scavenge or reuse treated medical items, and it shrinks the trash down so it's easier to haul away to a landfill. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h5)

question: What substance is commonly mixed with pharmaceutical waste during encapsulation to lock it away safely?

options.A: Cement mortar or bitumen
options.B: Dry river sand
options.C: Cooking vegetable oil
options.D: Pure liquid mercury

explanation: Encapsulation uses solidifying agents like cement to lock hazardous drugs into a solid block, keeping them from leaking into the environment. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h6)

question: When is chemical disinfection most commonly used in a healthcare facility?

options.A: For treating liquid infectious waste and laboratory cultures
options.B: For packaging expired patient food trays
options.C: For disposing of heavy metal surgical instruments
options.D: For processing large wooden crates and office furniture

explanation: Liquid waste and lab cultures are often treated directly with chemical disinfectants to make them safe before they go down the sewer lines. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h6)

question: What unsafe habit is known as the top cause of accidental needle-stick injuries among nurses?

options.A: Carrying a syringe in a uniform pocket
options.B: Cleaning floors with cold water
options.C: Recapping needles by hand after use
options.D: Using plastic yellow waste bags

explanation: Never try to recap a needle with your bare hands! That split second of trying to guide it back in is when most accidental pricks happen. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h7)

question: You just finished giving an injection. What should you do immediately with the used syringe and needle?

options.A: Remove the needle carefully with bare fingers and throw it in the dustbin
options.B: Drop the entire unit straight into the puncture-proof sharps container
options.C: Place the needle on the bedside table until the end of the shift
options.D: Break the needle in half to save space inside the disposal box

explanation: Drop the whole un-recapped syringe and needle right into your safety box. No taking parts apart, no bending—just straight in! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h7)

question: What key engineering feature protects underground water sources underneath a proper sanitary landfill?

options.A: Open drainage ditches filled with gravel
options.B: Deep burning pits without concrete walls
options.C: Direct connection to municipal storm water pipes
options.D: Impermeable bottom liners and leachate collection systems

explanation: Special heavy-duty bottom liners and drainage pipes catch contaminated liquids (leachate) so they don't soak down into our drinking water table. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h8)

question: Why is open dumping of raw, untreated medical waste a terrible practice?

options.A: It turns the surrounding soil overly fertile for farming crops
options.B: It produces excessive amounts of clean drinking water
options.C: It causes municipal electricity generators to overheat rapidly
options.D: It spreads infectious diseases and attracts pests like rodents and flies

explanation: Leaving clinical trash out in the open invites rats, flies, and stray animals to carry dangerous germs right into our communities. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h8)

question: Which vaccination is considered a mandatory occupational health requirement for healthcare workers handling clinical waste?

options.A: Hhepatitis B
options.B: Yellow fever only
options.C: Rabies
options.D: Cholera

explanation: Hepatitis B immunization protects clinical personnel from bloodborne viral transmission following occupational exposure incidents. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h9)

question: Why should you wear heavy-duty utility gloves instead of thin examination gloves when carrying waste bags?

options.A: They provide greater puncture and tear resistance against hidden sharp objects
options.B: They prevent hands from sweating in hot tropical weather
options.C: They allow healthcare workers to touch patient wounds directly
options.D: They are cheaper to purchase in large wholesale quantities

explanation: Utility gloves are thick and tough. They act as a strong physical barrier against stray needles or sharp trash that might poke through thin exam gloves. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h9)

question: Which Nigerian agency is responsible for enforcing environmental protection and waste regulations?

options.A: NCC
options.B: NAPTIP
options.C: NESREA
options.D: FRSC

explanation: NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) is the body making sure environmental laws and waste rules are followed across Nigeria. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h10)

question: Why do Nigerian healthcare facilities need a clear waste management plan and ongoing staff training?

options.A: To reduce the number of patients visiting outpatient departments
options.B: To bridge the gap between written safety policies and actual clinical practice
options.C: To eliminate the need for electricity in hospital laboratories
options.D: To qualify for international sports tournament sponsorships

explanation: Having a rulebook on paper isn't enough—training ensures everyone actually follows safe habits on the ward every single day! [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h10)
